name: Seventy-Seven
summary: Seventy-seven (or its multiplied form, four hundred ninety) appears at two sharply contrasting moments: Lamech's boast of unlimited revenge in Genesis, and Jesus' answer about unlimited forgiveness in Matthew -- widely read as Jesus deliberately echoing and inverting Lamech's number.

claims.text: Lamech declares that if Cain is avenged sevenfold, he himself will be avenged seventy-sevenfold -- an escalating boast of vengeance.

When Peter asks how many times he must forgive someone who sins against him, Jesus answers 'seventy-seven times' (some translations render this 'seventy times seven', i.e. four hundred ninety -- see the translation note below).

Jesus' answer to Peter is widely read as a deliberate echo of Lamech's number in Genesis 4:24, turning a boast of limitless revenge into a call to limitless forgiveness -- the same number, inverted in meaning. This is a literary/textual connection scholars draw between the two passages, not a claim either text makes explicitly about the other.

The Greek phrase behind Jesus' answer is genuinely ambiguous between two readings: 'seventy-seven times' (the rendering in the NIV, ESV, and NRSV) or 'seventy times seven', i.e. 490 (the rendering in the KJV and NKJV). Either way the point is the same -- a number too large to keep count of, not a literal ceiling -- but which exact number the original Greek intends is a real translation question, not settled by the text alone.

sources: sharethestruggle.org, 'Matthew 18:22: Why Jesus Said Forgive 77 Times'
